drug_class: Immunomodulatory agent (a type of cancer-fighting medicine)
purpose: Pomalidomide is used to treat a type of blood cancer called multiple myeloma, usually when other treatments have already been tried. It may also be used for a rare condition called Kaposi sarcoma. Your doctor prescribes it to help slow or stop the cancer from growing.
how_it_works: This medicine works in a few ways at once — it helps your immune system fight the cancer cells, it slows the growth of cancer cells directly, and it cuts off the blood supply that tumors need to survive. Think of it as boosting your body's defenses while also starving the cancer. It does not work like traditional chemotherapy, but it is still a powerful cancer treatment.
common_side_effects: Feeling very tired or weak, low blood cell counts (which can cause infections, bruising, or anemia), nausea, constipation, shortness of breath, dizziness, back pain, and fever. Many patients also notice swelling in the arms or legs.
warnings: This medicine can cause very serious birth defects — it must NEVER be used during pregnancy, and both men and women must use strict birth control. It is only available through a special safety program called REMS. It also raises your risk of dangerous blood clots, so tell your doctor right away if you have leg pain, chest pain, or trouble breathing. Your blood counts will need to be checked regularly because this drug can lower them significantly.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 4 mg taken by mouth once a day on days 1 through 21 of a 28-day cycle, then you take a week off. It is always taken on an empty stomach or at least 2 hours after a meal. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how your body responds and your blood test results.
